# Camera Pose and Parameter Optimization

Also called: Bundle Adjustment in NeRF, Joint Pose and NeRF Optimization, NeRF with Unknown Camera Parameters

## Overview
This family of methods addresses the problem of optimizing [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) scene representations when input camera poses are inaccurate, unknown, or when intrinsic parameters (such as focal length) are not provided. [Standard NeRF training](#985-nerf-training-loop-with-random-ray-batching.md) assumes perfect ground-truth camera poses; deviations from these poses cause the optimization to converge to incorrect geometry or fail entirely [S1]. These methods solve this by treating camera parameters as trainable variables within a fully differentiable pipeline, jointly minimizing the reconstruction loss with respect to both the [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) weights and the camera poses [S1]. They are distinguished from standard [training loops](#4290-training-loop.md) by the inclusion of pose update steps and specific strategies (such as coarse-to-fine scheduling or external priors) to stabilize the non-convex joint optimization landscape.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family share the core mechanism of differentiable rendering, where the gradient of the photometric loss with respect to the camera pose parameters flows back through the ray generation and [volume rendering equations](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md) to update the poses [S1].

**Parameterization:**
Camera poses are typically represented as rigid transformations $T_i \in SE(3)$, composed of a rotation matrix $R_i$ and a translation vector $t_i$ [S1]. To ensure valid rotations during optimization, $R_i$ is often parameterized using axis-angle vectors $\phi_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ or Lie algebra elements $\mathfrak{so}(3)$, converted to rotation matrices via Rodrigues' formula or the exponential map [S1]. Intrinsic parameters, such as focal length $f$, are treated as scalar trainable variables if unknown [S1].

**Optimization Structure:**
The joint optimization problem is solved using gradient-based methods (typically Adam) [S1]. Separate optimizers or distinct learning rates are commonly used for the NeRF network parameters $\Theta$ and the camera pose parameters to balance the convergence speeds of the complex scene representation and the geometric constraints [S1]. The loss function is primarily photometric, measuring the difference between rendered pixel colors $\hat{C}_i(p)$ and ground-truth image colors $I_i(p)$ [S1].

**Challenges:**
Joint optimization is highly non-convex and prone to local minima [S1]. Poor initialization can lead to divergence or incorrect intrinsics [S1]. Methods often employ strategies to mitigate this, such as coarse-to-fine frequency scheduling, external [depth priors](#7616-depth-regularization.md), or cascaded refinement stages.

## Subtopics

### [BARF (Bundle-Adjusting Neural Radiance Fields)](6872-barf-bundle-adjusting-neural-radiance-fields.md)
[BARF](#6872-barf-bundle-adjusting-neural-radiance-fields.md) reconstructs a NeRF from multi-view images when input camera poses contain errors. It addresses the sensitivity of [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) to pose inaccuracies by jointly optimizing network parameters and camera poses using a coarse-to-fine refinement strategy. Unlike methods that rely on external Structure-from-Motion (SfM) for initialization or assume perfect poses, BARF explicitly corrects pose errors during training by gradually introducing high-frequency [positional encoding](#876-positional-encoding.md) details.

### [NeRF with Unknown Camera Parameters](7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md)
[NeRF with Unknown Camera Parameters](#7405-nerf-with-unknown-camera-parameters.md) (NeRF--) is a method that jointly optimizes camera parameters along with a NeRF model on a sparse set of forward-facing views, eliminating the need for pre-estimated camera poses. Unlike baseline NeRF which requires ground-truth camera intrinsics and extrinsics, NeRF-- treats camera parameters as trainable variables within a fully differentiable pipeline, enabling joint optimization by minimizing the reconstruction loss. It sets itself apart from siblings like BARF by optimizing all camera parameters simultaneously from initialization, rather than using a coarse-to-fine frequency scheduling strategy.

### [L2G-NeRF](8671-l2g-nerf.md)
[L2G-NeRF](#8671-l2g-nerf.md) is a bundle-adjusting method that jointly optimizes neural 3D representations and camera poses by combining a local photometric alignment objective with a global geometric alignment objective. It solves the problem of recovering camera poses from poor initialization (e.g., identity matrices) where standard parametric methods diverge and non-parametric methods violate geometric constraints. Unlike its sibling [BARF](6872-barf-bundle-adjusting-neural-radiance-fields.md), which optimizes global poses directly, L2G-NeRF uses a differentiable local-to-global registration process that is more robust to large initial misalignments.

### [NoPe-NeRF](8705-nope-nerf.md)
[NoPe-NeRF](#8705-nope-nerf.md) is a method for training [Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)](#1576-neural-volume-rendering.md) without precomputed camera poses by integrating undistorted monocular depth priors. It addresses the challenge of optimizing camera parameters and scene geometry jointly by generating a dense point cloud from a monocular depth estimation network and constraining relative poses between consecutive frames. Unlike methods that rely solely on photometric consistency or coarse SfM initialization, NoPe-NeRF explicitly corrects scale and shift parameters during training to stabilize optimization in challenging camera trajectories.

### [AltNeRF](8763-altnerf.md)
[AltNeRF](#8763-altnerf.md) is a framework for creating resilient Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) representations from monocular videos without relying on known camera poses. It solves the problem of suboptimal NeRF reconstruction caused by imprecise initial camera poses and lack of explicit 3D supervision by using an alternating algorithm to harmonize NeRF outputs with self-supervised monocular depth estimation (SMDE) priors. Unlike methods that strictly align rendered depth with depth priors, AltNeRF uses error-tolerant regularization because the depth prior itself is not precise, allowing it to progressively refine both the scene geometry and camera poses.

### [CBARF](9066-cbarf.md)
CBARF is a 3D reconstruction model that optimizes imperfect camera poses using a cascaded bundle-adjustment (BA) structure to progressively refine poses and rectify erroneous ones. It builds on [BARF](6872-barf-bundle-adjusting-neural-radiance-fields.md) by introducing a coarse-to-fine optimization strategy with distinct stages, allowing it to handle larger initial pose errors (e.g., 30.4° rotation deviation) where standard BARF may overfit or diverge.

#### NeRF Registration
- **Definition:** A rigid NeRF registration method that minimizes a photometric loss between rendered images from two NeRFs, using VF and Normalizing Flows to guide ray sampling and generate novel views [S1].
- **Steps:** Optimize a 6-DoF rigid transformation parameter (rotation and translation) to align the two NeRFs [S1]. Minimize a photometric loss (Equation 7 in the full paper) between rendered images from the aligned NeRFs [S1]. Use VF and Normalizing Flows to sample novel camera viewpoints and guide ray sampling during optimization [S1].
- **Parameters:** Learnable scale factor (added to the 6-DoF parameters to handle unknown scale and illumination changes between scenes) [S1].
- **Pitfalls:** Photometric loss is susceptible to inaccuracies on textureless surfaces [S1]. High symmetry can cause convergence to a partially accurate solution that deviates by 180° from the true solution [S1]. Partial overlap or moving objects are not explicitly handled and may cause failure [S1].

#### Hybrid 2D/3D Registration Optimization Pipeline
- **Definition:** A two-stage optimization pipeline for 2D/3D registration that first minimizes a differentiable network similarity loss ($L_N$) for global convergence, then switches to a traditional Grad-NCC loss ($L_{GNNC}$) for local refinement [S2].
- **Steps:** Initialize pose parameters $\theta$. Optimize over $L_N$ using SGD with cyclic learning rate between $1e-6$ and $1e-4$ every 100 steps and momentum 0.9 [S2]. Monitor convergence by calculating the standard deviation of $L_N$ over the last 10 iterations ($std_{L_N}$) [S2]. If $std_{L_N} < 3 \times 10^{-3}$, switch optimization to Grad-NCC similarity [S2]. Optimize over $L_{GNNC}$ using SGD with cyclic learning rate between $1e-3$ and $3e-3$ and momentum 0.9 [S2]. Stop when $std_{L_{GNNC}} < 1 \times 10^{-5}$ [S2].

#### Progressive Camera Pose Generation
- **Definition:** A training strategy that gradually increases the angular distance of sampled target viewpoints from source views to stabilize optimization [S3, unofficial].
- **Steps:** Sample noise uniformly from interval $[-\beta, +\beta]$ and add it to original Euler rotation angles of input view poses [S3, unofficial].
- **Parameters:** Parameter $\beta$: Grows linearly from 3 to 9 degrees throughout the course of optimization [S3, unofficial].

## Background
The problem of optimizing NeRFs with unknown or erroneous camera poses emerged as a limitation of the original NeRF framework, which required high-quality Structure-from-Motion (SfM) outputs [S1]. BARF (Bundle-Adjusting [Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md)) was one of the first methods to explicitly address this by introducing a coarse-to-fine frequency annealing strategy for positional encoding, allowing the network to first learn low-frequency scene structures robust to pose errors before refining details [S1]. Subsequent works like NeRF-- extended this to include intrinsic parameter optimization (focal length) without any pose initialization [S1]. L2G-NeRF introduced a local-to-global registration approach to handle identity initialization [S1]. More recent methods like NoPe-NeRF and AltNeRF incorporate monocular depth priors to provide geometric constraints for monocular video inputs, while CBARF enhances the BARF framework with a cascaded bundle adjustment structure to handle larger initial errors [S1].
